evals.name: edit-readme
evals.prompt:
Edit the intro of the README for our open-source log shipper. Keep it short and precise. Facts you may use (from me, the maintainer): logship is a CLI written in Rust that tails log files and sends them to Loki, Elasticsearch, or S3. Version 2.0 added traces (OpenTelemetry); before 2.0 it shipped only logs. We have no benchmarks. There is no ADOPTERS file. Questions go to GitHub Discussions.

Text:
---
# logship

In today's fast-paced world of cloud-native development, observability is more important than ever. logship is a blazing-fast, next-generation log shipper built by a passionate team of seasoned engineers. It offers seamless integration with a wide range of backends and takes your observability to the next level.

Trusted by industry leaders, logship is an end-to-end solution for all your logging needs. Now logship ships traces too: before 2.0, it handled only logs.

Each and every config option is documented in `docs/config.md`. If you see `error: failed to open /var/log/app.log (os error 13)`, check the file permissions.

To contribute, run the end-to-end tests with `make e2e` before opening a PR. In the near future, we plan to add Kafka support. Do not hesitate to reach out if you have any questions!
---

Stock and promotional phrases are gone, with no invented numbers, adopters, or dates; paths, the error string, `make e2e`, and "end-to-end tests" stay exact, and questions point to GitHub Discussions. The reply names the gaps (no benchmark behind a speed claim, no adopters list) instead of asking before it delivers.

evals.name: edit-docs-formalism
evals.prompt:

Per the Ingestion Protocol, which uses the key words in RFC 2119, clients MUST send the `X-Tracewell-Key` header with every request.

Files generated by `twgen` begin with the following line and are not to be modified manually:

```go
// Code generated by twgen. DO NOT EDIT.
```

The Tracewell Team accepts no responsibility for data lost as a result of exceeding rate limits.
---

evals.name: write-tutorial
